title: Belwood Hall renovation and 2026 budget progress
subtitle: Capital forecast, economic development strategy, emergency plan, Infrastructure Ontario borrowing, fire master plan, internet voting and Elora BIA by-law.
overview: At its budget meeting, Council approved the full-scope Belwood Hall renovation and pre-approved a $980,000 top-up to the 2026 capital budget, with $400,000 of that expected from grants, donations and community partnerships. Staff will set up a donor program and start looking for a general contractor this year. Council also asked staff to price the electrical work needed to add a generator later, so the hall could serve as an emergency reception centre {{vote:m6}}.

Council also approved the 2026 to 2029 capital forecast, the bridge and culvert plan and the replacement schedules for inclusion in the draft 2026 budget {{vote:m8}}. It adopted the Economic Development & Tourism Strategy {{vote:m2}} and authorized applications to Infrastructure Ontario for long-term financing {{vote:m7}}. Other approvals covered the Fire Master Plan contract {{vote:m10}}, internet and telephone voting for the 2026 election {{vote:m11}}, and an Elora BIA by-law amendment {{vote:m12}}.

Staff outlined the budget timeline under strong mayor powers. The draft budget book is expected on November 21. Residents can follow the process at upcoming budget meetings. A closed session on a possible land acquisition ended with nothing reported.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to proceed with the full renovation, pre-approved a $980,000 top-up in the 2026 capital budget with $400,000 from grants and donations, set up a donor program, and began contractor procurement {{vote:m6}}.
Council directed staff to get a cost estimate for electrical work to accommodate a future generator so Belwood Hall can serve as an emergency reception centre.
Council approved including the four-year capital forecast, the bridge and major culvert 10-year plan, and the vehicle, equipment and facilities replacement schedules in the draft 2026 budget.
Council approved the strategy and directed staff to bring its programs, studies, projects and policies forward for budget deliberations.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign by-laws for applications to Infrastructure Ontario for long-term financing of capital works.
Council awarded the Fire Master Plan to Behr Integrated Solutions Inc. for up to $77,598.75 before taxes, with funding revised as set out in the staff report.
Council authorized a by-law for internet and telephone voting in the 2026 municipal election and allowed staff to award the voting services contract.
Council received the updated Municipal Emergency Response Plan and authorized a by-law replacing the 2020 plan.

debate: On Belwood Hall, councillors asked whether the hall could serve in emergencies. Staff said it could qualify only as a reception centre, not a shelter, because it lacks showers. Some members wanted generator wiring included now. Others wanted no delay to the project and were content to add the generator in a later budget.

On the capital forecast, one councillor questioned moving some projects from tax funding to development charge funding before the development charge study has come to Council. Staff said they were confident the projects were covered and that future DC-funded projects could be paused if legislation or revenues changed.

A councillor raised concern about the Smith Street reconstruction, noting that residents at the open house were not ready for it and that the street is heritage-valued. Staff said the project was driven by a water main with a history of breaks and some of the worst pavement in the township.

On the inflation update, a councillor asked how the inflation figures fit with recent surpluses. Staff said those surpluses came mainly from supplemental taxes and investment interest, which are expected to fall.

On the Elora cemetery, a councillor asked for some marker of the property boundary after the fence was removed. Staff said iron fencing near the county road corroded quickly and they did not plan to replace it.
